q: Carbon is found in nature as ____ and graphite.
e: Diamond is one of the allotropes of carbon, known for its hardness.

q: Carbon can also be found as compounds combining with other elements in petroleum, coal, natural gas, limestone, carbon dioxide and ____ .
e: Sugar is an organic compound that contains carbon.

q: If an element can exist in more than one form, in the same physical state, it is said to exhibit ____ or polymorphism.
e: Allotropy refers to the existence of an element in different forms.

q: The different forms of an element in the same physical state that possess different physical properties are known as ____ of that element.
e: Allotropes have distinct physical and sometimes chemical properties.

q: Diamond, graphite, fullerene and graphene are ____ of carbon.
e: These are different structural forms of carbon.

q: In diamond, each carbon atom is surrounded by ____ other carbon atoms.
e: This tetrahedral arrangement contributes to diamond's strength.

q: Diamond has a giant structure containing millions of carbon atoms in a three dimensional network of strong carbon-carbon ____ .
e: Covalent bonds are strong connections between atoms.

q: Diamond is very hard and has a very high melting point of ____ °C.
e: This high melting point is due to the strong covalent bonds in diamond.

q: Graphite is soft due to its layered structure where each carbon atom is surrounded by ____ other carbon atoms in the same plane.
e: This planar arrangement allows layers to slide over each other.

q: Graphite has a soapy touch and can act as a ____ due to its layered structure.
e: Graphite's layered structure allows it to reduce friction.

q: Graphite is a good conductor of electricity and heat due to the presence of ____ electrons.
e: Free electrons allow graphite to conduct electricity.

q: The melting point of graphite is ____ °C.
e: Graphite has a high melting point due to strong covalent bonds.

q: Fullerene (C60) is an allotrope of carbon in the form of a hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes and sizes. Spherical fullerenes are also referred to as ____ balls.
e: Bucky balls are a specific type of fullerene.

q: Graphene is a single layer (monolayer) of graphite and is tightly bound in a ____ ring structure.
e: Hexagonal arrangements are characteristic of graphene's structure.

q: Graphene is about ____ times stronger than the strongest steel.
e: Graphene's strength-to-weight ratio is exceptionally high.

q: Graphene is a transparent and flexible conductor widely used for various material/device applications, including solar cells, light-emitting diodes (LED), touch panels and ____ windows or phones.
e: Smart devices utilize graphene for its conductive properties.

q: Charcoal is made by heating wood in the absence of ____ .
e: This process prevents combustion and results in charcoal.

q: Coal is found in nature and is a black heavy ____ .
e: Coal is a naturally occurring fossil fuel.

q: Coke is formed by heating coal in the absence of ____ .
e: Coke is a purer form of carbon used in various applications.

q: Carbon black (soot) is a black powder formed when kerosene is burnt in a limited amount of ____ .
e: Limited air supply leads to incomplete combustion, producing soot.

q: When carbon burns in excess air or oxygen, carbon dioxide is formed. Carbon monoxide is formed when carbon burns in a ____ amount of air or oxygen.
e: Limited oxygen leads to incomplete combustion, producing carbon monoxide.

q: Carbon can be used as a reducing agent in the extraction of some metals. When strongly heated, carbon can reduce the oxides of zinc and other metals such as CuO, PbO and ____ to their respective metals.
e: Iron(III) oxide can be reduced by carbon to produce iron.

q: Carbon + oxygen (excess) -> ____ .
e: This reaction represents complete combustion of carbon.

q: Carbon + oxygen (limited) -> ____ .
e: This reaction represents incomplete combustion of carbon.
